rows.title: VR-4 4WS Rear Steering Pump and Hard Line Leaks
rows.howToFix: Inspect the flanged feed/return line at the rear pump for rust and weeping. For small low-pressure leaks, cut out the corroded section and bridge with high-pressure hose and double-clamped fittings as a temporary fix. For high-pressure-side or pump-internal leaks, the proper repair requires dropping the rear subframe to access the pump (parts ~$900 OEM, labor 6-10 hours). Many long-term VR-4 owners install a 4WS delete kit with block-off plates that bypasses the rear pump and hard-locks the rear steering rack, eliminating the failure point entirely ($150-$400 in parts).

rows.title: 4G63 7-Bolt Crank Walk (Thrust Bearing Failure)
rows.howToFix: Confirm with a dial indicator on the crank snout while a helper presses the clutch (>0.010" axial movement = crank walk). The only durable fix is to pull the engine, replace the crankshaft, all main/rod/thrust bearings, and ideally install ARP main studs with dowels. Mitigation while diagnosing: verify clutch master/slave cylinder adjustment so there is zero residual pressure on the throwout bearing at rest, and disable the clutch interlock switch so drivers do not rest a foot on the clutch. Plugging the 7-bolt piston oil squirters is a common preventive modification during a rebuild.

rows.title: Infotainment System Freezing and Connectivity Issues
rows.howToFix: Update to the latest firmware via USB or dealer. Perform a factory reset to clear corrupted data. Use wired connections for CarPlay/Android Auto if wireless connections are unreliable.

rows.title: Phantom / False Automatic Emergency Braking (Forward Collision Mitigation)
rows.howToFix: Update the ADAS/FCM software at the dealer and have the front radar and windshield-mounted camera inspected, cleaned, and recalibrated. Drivers can temporarily disable Forward Collision Mitigation where false activations are dangerous, but a software update/recalibration is the proper remedy.

rows.title: Spontaneous Windshield and Door Glass Cracking (4th-Gen Thin Glass)
rows.howToFix: No recall or TSB addresses the glass quality; replacement is the only fix. Owners use insurance/comprehensive glass coverage. rows.title: AC Compressor Premature Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace the AC compressor, receiver/drier, and expansion valve. Flush the entire system to remove metal particles. Install an inline filter on the liquid line to protect the new compressor from residual debris.

rows.title: CVT Judder and Hesitation
rows.howToFix: Replace the CVT fluid with Mitsubishi DiaQueen CVTF-J4 every 30,000 miles. A TCM reprogram may smooth out the shift calibration. Avoid towing with the CVT-equipped models.

rows.title: CVT shudder, slipping, and premature failure
rows.howToFix: Replace CVT fluid on a shortened interval (roughly every 30,000-60,000 miles rather than 'lifetime'). Persistent shudder may require a valve body or full CVT replacement. Earlier model years had a separate recall (16V-563) for a CVT control module causing delayed gear engagement.
rows.dispositionReason: At least one replacement is conditional on a stated diagnostic result.

rows.title: Underbody and Subframe Rust/Corrosion
rows.howToFix: Apply rust-proofing undercoating annually in salt-belt areas. Inspect the rear subframe for structural integrity during routine maintenance. Replace corroded brake lines with stainless steel or coated replacements.
